interpretation_limits: Associations do not prove that large norm causes errors or that normalization will improve detection. Full normalization can remove amplitude useful to distinguish anomalies; low-norm missed anomalies and same-class/same-range normal contrasts must also be considered. Synthetic modified backgrounds recur across chosen views, so points are not independent repetitions.

decision.full_input_normalization: Not established as a necessary fix: most normal false positives are below the training99th-percentile norm, and class/range-controlled associations have mixed directions.
decision.limited_experiment: If one small controlled experiment is pursued, normalize only the residual-branch input while preserving the original whitened feature skip path and all training/development populations. The evidence is strongest for nearby fence observations, not a universal norm failure.
decision.reason_to_preserve_amplitude: Detected synthetic anomalies have higher whitened median norm than missed anomalies; erasing all magnitude can remove useful evidence.
decision.causal_status: Association diagnosis only; no normalization intervention has been evaluated.
